newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Jakarta stocks end higher on property and banks.
newsitem.headline: Jakarta stocks end higher on property and banks.

text.p: Jakarta stocks ended higher on Thursday on sustained buying interest in property and banking stocks, brokers said.
"But overall trading was directionless. The market seems loose," said Jordan Zulkarnaen, an analyst with Pentasena Securities.
The Jakarta Composite Index close 2.18 points, or 0.32 percent higher at 695.22 points. Gainers led losers by 65 to 62, with 73 counters unchanged. Total turn-over was about 403 billion rupiah.

"Some property stocks had touched the bottom. On an average, they were was discounted about 50 to 60 percent against net asset values. Technically, their prices should increase now," another analyst said.
However, both analysts said, active trading seen on Thursday in some property counters was due to individual rumours.
Bank Negara Indonesia, Bank International Indonesia and Unibank were among other active stocks.
Analysts said the declining trend in deposit rates combined with relatively stable lending rates had improved sentiment on banking stocks as they could maintain higher profit margins.
